text:
sqlpipe moves data from Postgres to S3 in three stages, connected by streaming buffers instead of temporary files.

A reader process queries Postgres and streams rows in batches. It never loads the full result set into memory.

A converter reads these batches and builds Parquet row groups. Each row group holds one batch, so conversion runs at a steady, predictable memory cost.

An uploader writes each row group to S3 as part of a multipart upload. If a part fails, the uploader retries it without restarting the whole upload.

The three stages run concurrently. The reader, converter, and uploader each process a different batch at the same time, so pipeline throughput depends on the slowest stage, not on the sum of all stages.
